title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
lead: AgentSSL treats semi-supervised learning as a search over executable programs. The researchers examine two different challenges: whether agents can discover strong methods from scarce labels and abundant unlabeled data, and whether those methods can be selected reliably without trustworthy validation.
question: Can agents find a strong learning strategy when labeled examples are scarce?

signals.label: Settings with stronger discovered programs
signals.detail: The strongest agent-discovered programs outperform the best human-designed SSL baselines in eight of twelve evaluated settings. These are oracle-selected results.

signals.label: Largest reported improvement
signals.detail: The largest improvement reported over a strong human SSL baseline occurs in an individual dataset and label setting. It is not an average gain across tasks.

signals.label: Selection can erase gains
signals.detail: The authors report up to a 47% performance drop when their agent feedback metric is used to select a program, rather than an oracle choosing the strongest.

signals.label: Evaluated program instances
signals.detail: ProgramSelectBench collects agent-generated and human-designed SSL programs across six classification datasets, enabling further selection research.

insight.label: OPEN RESEARCH PROBLEM
insight.title: Discovering a strong program is not the same as selecting one.
insight.detail: The paper separates search quality from choosing a deployable program without trustworthy labeled validation. It also describes challenges transferring agent-discovered SSL strategies into real ecology detection tasks.
